what: a long modelled external thread: M6 over a 24 mm shaft (24 turns), the kind that once ran out of depth in the boolean
method: ISO 68-1 basic profile: H = P sqrt3/2, basic depth 5H/8. External groove (the space between teeth): a trapezoid P/4 wide at the root radius d/2 - 5H/8, widening by 2 tan30 per unit of radius to 7P/8 at d/2. Internal groove: P/8 wide at the major radius d/2, widening to 3P/4 at the minor radius, cut only where there is material (r >= hole radius). Pappus: volume per turn = 2 pi A rc (A the trapezoid area, rc its centroid radius from the axis); a helical sweep of L/P turns removes exactly (L/P) x that, where each end of the thread is a free end or lies inside material. Shaft R=3.0 L=24, M6 (P=1.0) over its whole length, both ends free: V = pi R^2 L - (L/P) V_turn = 678.5840 - 24 x 5.31713 = 550.9729 mm3. COM on the axis at L/2 (12): the groove is symmetric over whole turns. Tolerance 1%: a modelled thread is a faceted helical solid (radial chord error up to 1% of the pitch on every wall, i.e. a volume deficit of about 4/3 x sag/R).
